acceptance_criteria: The declared input domain matches the specified field names, types and bounds.
obligations.statement: The input is an object with events, start, end, width and fill; each event has a string group, integer time and integer or null value. start and end are integers, width is a positive integer, fill is 'none' or 'previous', and start <= end.

acceptance_criteria: previous is initially unset independently for each group.
A count-positive bucket outputs its sum and updates previous even when its sum is zero.
A count-zero bucket leaves previous unchanged.
Pre-start events cannot seed previous.
scope: ascending bucket processing within each group

source_refs.interpretation: Nonempty bucket value and previous update.
Zero is a valid previous sum.

obligations.statement: Within each group, previous begins unset and tracks the sum of the latest earlier bucket with count greater than zero. Processing a nonempty bucket sets its value and previous to its sum, including zero; empty buckets preserve previous. Events before start never initialize previous.

acceptance_criteria: solution.py exposes solve(data).
Repeated calls with equivalent inputs produce identical results without observable side effects.
The result is JSON-serializable.
obligations.statement: Provide a pure deterministic Python 3 solve(data) function in solution.py accepting JSON-compatible Python input and returning a JSON-serializable value.

acceptance_criteria: Groups equal the lexicographically sorted set of group names in events.
Out-of-range events still contribute group names.
An empty events list yields no groups and an empty result.
obligations.statement: Determine groups from every event's group name, deduplicate names and sort them lexicographically, retaining groups whose events are all outside the requested range.

acceptance_criteria: Every group has exactly the specified ascending bucket starts.
The final bucket is clipped at end.
start = end yields no buckets.
A time at a bucket's upper endpoint belongs to the following bucket if present; a time equal to end belongs to no bucket.

source_refs.interpretation: Bucket start progression for each group.
Strict endpoint limit and half-open bucket coverage.

obligations.statement: For each group generate bucket starts start + k*width for all nonnegative integers k whose starts are strictly below end. Each bucket covers [bucketStart,min(bucketStart+width,end)).

acceptance_criteria: count equals the number of qualifying event occurrences.
sum equals the exact integer sum of qualifying values.
Null values and times outside [start,end) contribute neither sum nor count.
Duplicate occurrences contribute independently.
A bucket containing only null-valued events has count zero.

source_refs.interpretation: Count uses the same qualifying values.

obligations.statement: For each bucket sum and count all events of its group whose times fall in the bucket and whose values are non-null. Count each duplicate event occurrence separately.

acceptance_criteria: fill 'none' produces null for every empty bucket.
fill 'previous' uses the latest preceding nonempty bucket sum.
Empty buckets before the first nonempty bucket output null.
A preceding sum of zero fills subsequent empty buckets with zero.

source_refs.interpretation: Fill modes and initial null behavior.

obligations.statement: An empty bucket outputs null under fill 'none'. Under fill 'previous', it outputs the latest previous nonempty bucket sum for the same group, or null if none exists.

acceptance_criteria: Each record has the specified group name, bucket start, qualifying count and computed value.
The list preserves group then bucket ordering.
The specified input and output structures are preserved.
obligations.statement: Return a list of objects with exactly group, start, count and value fields, one per generated group bucket, ordered first by lexicographic group and then ascending bucket start.

acceptance_criteria: The first example returns exactly the three specified a-group records.
The second example returns exactly the specified z-group record.

source_refs.interpretation: Concrete zero-sum carry-forward and pre-start exclusion examples.

obligations.statement: Match both public examples: the a-group zero-sum bucket has count 2 and value 0 followed by empty buckets at starts 2 and 4 with value 0; the z-group with only a pre-start event has a single bucket at start 0 with count 0 and value null.

acceptance_criteria: No third-party library is required.
Execution performs no external I/O.
obligations.statement: Use only the Python standard library and perform no external I/O.
